summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as mode 1777 (drwxrwxrwt) root:root — a shared writable directory with the sticky bit set so any user can create files but only the owner (or root) can remove/rename them. Persisted the configuration across reboots via /etc/tmpfiles.d/srv-drop.conf. Verified the behavior functionally with two throwaway test users both before and after a full node restart of node1, confirming the boot identity changed (real reboot, not just a service bounce) and that the directory and sticky-bit enforcement survived intact.
actions_performed: Created /srv/drop, set ownership root:root and mode 1777 (sticky bit + world writable)
Added /etc/tmpfiles.d/srv-drop.conf to persist directory mode/ownership across reboots
Created two temporary Linux users (dropuserA, dropuserB) to functionally test sticky-bit enforcement
Verified dropuserB could write its own file but could not delete dropuserA's file (Operation not permitted), while dropuserA could delete its own file
Cleaned up test files and removed the temporary test users
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id and healthy /srv/drop permissions
Issued a native reboot (systemctl reboot) on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned, confirming a changed boot_id proving an actual restart occurred
Re-verified /srv/drop permissions (1777 root:root) survived the restart
Re-ran the two-user cross-delete test post-restart to confirm sticky-bit protection still functions, then cleaned up test users/files again

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop created as shared writable directory (mode 1777, root:root)
evidence.summary: mkdir + chown + chmod 1777 applied; stat confirms 1777 root:root

evidence.requirement: Sticky bit enforcement: users cannot remove files owned by other users (pre-restart proof)
evidence.summary: Created dropuserA/dropuserB, dropuserA wrote fileA.txt, dropuserB's attempt to delete it failed with 'Operation not permitted' (exit 1), while dropuserA's own delete succeeded (exit 0)
Wrote /etc/tmpfiles.d/srv-drop.conf with 'd /srv/drop 1777 root root -' to enforce/recreate the directory mode on boot

evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline and boot identity
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id be303eb3-eeb6-4466-86f1-fd6406dd7dad and confirmed /srv/drop at 1777 root:root before restart
systemctl reboot issued via backgrounded nohup so acknowledgement returned before disconnect

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proof via changed boot identity
evidence.summary: Connection dropped during reboot (timeout/reset), then exec succeeded again with new boot_id 23fd1542-85c5-48a5-a73b-351cc61b1b88, proving an actual restart distinct from the pre-restart boot_id

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop configuration and data
evidence.summary: Post-reboot stat/ls confirms /srv/drop still mode 1777 root:root (drwxrwxrwt)

evidence.requirement: Post-restart functional re-verification of sticky-bit enforcement
evidence.summary: Fresh test users recreated post-reboot: cross-user delete failed (Operation not permitted, exit 1), owner delete succeeded (exit 0), confirming behavior survived the restart; test users/files cleaned up afterward
